Here's the thing: the image decoder doesn't have to be complicated. You just have to respect it. And the result? A lean, mean image decoder — two hundred lines of pure, battle-tested C.

So I did what any stubborn programmer would do — I tore the whole thing down and **rewrote it from scratch**. Picture this: it's 2 a.m., the coffee is cold, and my image decoder has just crashed — again.

Why does this keep happening? I'll tell you why. Because we trust abstractions we have never read! The lesson? Never underestimate the power of simple code. Trust me, you'll thank yourself later.
